results.summary: This project implements a multiplication and accumulation (MAC) operation in Verilog. It takes two 8-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit output, likely the accumulated result. The documentation is minimal, stating only that it multiplies and accumulates data, and suggests testing with a memory operation. No external hardware is specified, and the design's exact behavior and interface are not fully described.

TinyQV is a small RISC-V SoC implementing the RV32EC instruction set with Zcb and Zicond extensions, using QSPI flash for program storage and QSPI PSRAM for data memory. It includes a UART and SPI controller, and is intended to be used with a QSPI PMOD containing flash and RAM, as well as an ST7789 LCD display and game controller. The design has been tested on silicon and works at up to 98 MHz, running CoreMark and MicroPython. It requires specific reset and initialization sequences, and external hardware such as the QSPI PMOD and optionally buttons.

The SkyKing Demo generates an RGB222 VGA signal to display an animation of a plane flying into the sunset with text. It runs automatically and requires a VGA PMOD connected to the output pins. The design is a simple demo with no interactive inputs. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand its function and hardware needs.

This project implements a 32-bit floating point adder accessible over SPI, with four internal registers that can be read and written. It uses a simple command-based SPI protocol and requires an external SPI master, such as an Arduino, for testing. The designer notes that it did not work with standard Arduino SPI controllers, possibly due to bugs in the SPI receive logic. The design is a specialized arithmetic unit for floating-point operations.

This is a 4-bit ALU that performs arithmetic and logical operations on two 4-bit inputs based on a 4-bit opcode. It outputs an 8-bit result and provides carry-out and overflow status flags. The design is purely combinational and can be tested by applying various opcodes and inputs. The documentation includes a testing procedure but is somewhat unclear about the exact operations supported.

This project is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit numbers to produce an 8-bit product. It is implemented using a manual structural design with AND gates and full adders. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. Testing can be done by editing a Python test script to add custom test cases.

This project implements a digital leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron with four weight inputs and a spike input, producing a spike output. It uses reset by subtraction and has configurable leakage and threshold. The design is purely digital and requires no external hardware. Testing involves applying weights and spikes to observe spiking behavior. The documentation is minimal but indicates the core functionality.

This project implements a simple XOR cipher with UART communication. It receives an 8-bit character over UART, XORs it with a key, and transmits the result back. The key can be updated via a dedicated input pin, with a default key of 0xAA. It requires a 50 MHz clock and uses UART pins for communication. The design is straightforward and can be tested with a serial terminal.

This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit numbers to produce an 8-bit product. It uses AND gates to generate partial products and full adders to sum them. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. A Cocotb testbench is provided to verify its functionality with various test cases.

This project is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit inputs to produce an 8-bit product. It is built using AND gates and full adders in a manual structural design. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. Testing can be done by applying input values and observing the output product.
